# index.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# pricewright

Price services and products from a model of their costs and effort, not from a market median. Travel is an explicit add-on, a whole rate card is checked for consistency, and market comparables are a separate, swappable input.

```bash
pip install pricewright
pricewright card my-card.yaml -o card.md      # price, check, compare, render
pricewright travel 3.5 --transport 220 --travellers 2 --day-rate 900
pricewright specialties                       # templates, and the research each needs
```

```python
from pricewright import price, Rates
from pricewright.specialties.training import talk, private_workshop

rates = Rates({"founder": 900})                       # target day rate, 7 h a day
q = price(talk(delivery="online"), rates)
q.unit_price, q.hours_total, q.effective_day           # 1700, 11.2, ~1058
```

## Why

A rate card assembled from different market medians contradicts itself. You get a 60-minute talk at 10,000 next to a 6,000 private day, and “the market says so” explains nothing to whoever has to defend the number. pricewright builds each price from **who works how long** (development amortised over the runs you expect to sell, prep, delivery, admin, feedback) and **what it costs** (credits, venue, tools, fees). It adds contingency and margin, then rounds. Every metric is then recomputed from the printed price: the effective day rate per hour actually worked, the price per contact hour and per person-hour, and the seats needed to pay the target rate.

## Layers

| Module           | What it does                                                                                                                                               |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `base`           | `Rates`, `Effort`, `Cost`, `Offering` (frozen dataclasses), `day_rate_from_income`                                                                         |
| `model`          | `price(offering, rates)` turns an offering into a `Quote` with the full arithmetic                                                                         |
| `travel`         | `travel_addon(Trip, policy=TravelPolicy())`: time beyond 1 h each way at half rate, nights by rule, expenses at cost                                       |
| `ratecard`       | `check_card(quotes)`: effective-rate spread, dominance, private vs seats, online vs on site, volume per hour                                               |
| `research`       | load comparables packets (YAML), normalise them (per person-hour, per contact hour, per finished minute), place a price at an evidence-weighted percentile |
| `specialties`    | registry of templates: `training`, `av_production`, `software`; adding a specialty means adding one module                                                 |
| `spec`, `report` | a YAML rate card in, a Markdown card with its rationale out                                                                                                |

Baseline research packets (dated 2026-10) ship in `pricewright/data/packets/`. Refresh them before quoting a real client.

## The agent skill

`pricewright/data/skills/pricing-expert/` is the `pricing-expert` skill. It routes an offering to a specialty, states the research it needs, and explains the method and the trade practice of each field. Its references cover training, travel, audiovisual production and software (subscriptions, usage, credits, seats, tiers). It is `gh skill`-discoverable and ships with `pip install`.

## A spec

```yaml
title: My rate card
currency: EUR
rates: {day_rates: {founder: 900}, hours_per_day: 7}
market: {packets: [training-2026-10.yaml], fx: {USD: 0.86, GBP: 1.15}}
travel:
  scenarios:
    - {name: "2 h by train, 2 people", trip: {one_way_hours: 2, transport_round_trip: 150, travellers: 2}}
sensitivity: {day_rates: [700, 900, 1100]}
offerings:
  - {id: talk, specialty: training, template: talk, params: {delivery: online}}
  - {id: day, specialty: training, template: private_workshop, params: {group: 12}}
  - {id: spot, specialty: av_production, template: production, params: {style: commercial, seconds: 30}}
```

A complete example is `pricewright/data/skills/pricing-expert/references/example-spec.yaml`.

# _autosummary/pricewright.base.html.md

# pricewright.base

The data model of a price: who works how long, what it costs, and on what terms.

Everything here is a frozen dataclass, so an offering is a value you can build,
compare, serialise and re-price. The arithmetic lives in [`pricewright.model`](_autosummary/pricewright.model.html.md#module-pricewright.model).

Vocabulary:

- an [`Effort`](_autosummary/pricewright.base.html.md#pricewright.base.Effort) line is hours of one role, spent per *run* of the offering,
  per *participant*, or once for *development* (amortised over the expected runs);
- a [`Cost`](_autosummary/pricewright.base.html.md#pricewright.base.Cost) line is money paid to someone else (credits, venue, materials),
  with the same three bases;
- an [`Offering`](_autosummary/pricewright.base.html.md#pricewright.base.Offering) bundles them with the commercial frame: unit of sale,
  delivery mode, contact hours, seats, fees, contingency and margin;
- [`Rates`](_autosummary/pricewright.base.html.md#pricewright.base.Rates) holds the provider’s own economics (the day rate per role).

|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

A freelancer or a two-person studio bills far fewer days than it works: selling,
admin, development and gaps eat the rest. `billable_days` is that real number,
not 220.

```pycon

700
```

# _autosummary/pricewright.html.md

# pricewright

pricewright: price services and products from a model of their costs and effort.

Simple things simple:

```default
>>> from pricewright import price, Rates
>>> from pricewright.specialties.training import talk
>>> q = price(talk(delivery="online"), Rates({"founder": 900}))
>>> q.unit_price > 0
True
```

A whole rate card, checked for consistency and compared with a market packet:

```default
from pricewright import load_spec, build_card, render
print(render(build_card(load_spec("card.yaml"))))
```

Layers: [`base`](_autosummary/pricewright.base.html.md#module-pricewright.base) (data), [`model`](_autosummary/pricewright.model.html.md#module-pricewright.model) (the arithmetic),
[`travel`](_autosummary/pricewright.travel.html.md#module-pricewright.travel) (on-site add-on), [`ratecard`](_autosummary/pricewright.ratecard.html.md#module-pricewright.ratecard) (card-wide
checks), [`research`](_autosummary/pricewright.research.html.md#module-pricewright.research) (market packets), [`specialties`](_autosummary/pricewright.html.md#pricewright.specialties)
(templates per kind of offering, in a registry), [`spec`](_autosummary/pricewright.spec.html.md#module-pricewright.spec) and
[`report`](_autosummary/pricewright.report.html.md#module-pricewright.report) (YAML in, Markdown out).

### pricewright.position(value, comparables, , metric='per_person_contact_hour', fx=None, currency='EUR')

Locate `value` (already in `metric` units and `currency`) among comparables.

`fx` maps a currency to its value in `currency` (e.g. `{"USD": 0.87}` when
`currency='EUR'`). A comparable in a currency missing from `fx` is skipped
rather than silently treated as equal.

```pycon
>>> cs = [Comparable(str(i), "training", "x", price=p, unit="per_person",
...                  contact_hours=1, evidence="fetched") for i, p in enumerate([40, 50, 60, 70, 80])]
>>> position(65, cs).verdict, position(65, cs).median
('within market', 60.0)
```

* **Return type:**

# _autosummary/pricewright.model.html.md

# pricewright.model

The cost-and-effort model: from an [`Offering`](_autosummary/pricewright.base.html.md#pricewright.base.Offering) to a price.

The formula, per run of the offering:

```default
labour   = sum(hours x hourly rate)        # development hours / amortize_runs,
                                           # participant hours x participants
direct   = sum(third-party costs, with markup)
base     = (labour + direct) x (1 + contingency)
net      = base / (1 - margin)             # margin is a share of the price
revenue  = (net + fixed fees x transactions) / (1 - fees_pct)
revenue *= positioning                     # a stated launch discount or premium
unit price = revenue / participants_expected   (open, per-person sales)
           = revenue                          (everything else)
```

then the unit price is rounded (`rounder=`) and every metric (effective rate per
hour worked, price per contact hour, break-even seats) is recomputed from the
*rounded* price, so the rationale describes the number actually printed.

### Functions

| [`price`](_autosummary/pricewright.model.html.md#pricewright.model.price)(offering[, rates, rounder])   | Price one offering from its effort and costs.   |

# _autosummary/pricewright.ratecard.html.md

# pricewright.ratecard

Consistency across a whole rate card.

A single price can be defended on its own and still be absurd next to its
neighbours (the 10,000 talk next to a 6,000 private day). These checks look at
the card as a whole. Each returns [`Finding`](_autosummary/pricewright.ratecard.html.md#pricewright.ratecard.Finding) objects; [`check_card()`](_autosummary/pricewright.ratecard.html.md#pricewright.ratecard.check_card)
runs them all. A check is any `Callable[[Sequence[Quote]], Iterable[Finding]]`,
so a specialty can add its own (`checks=`).

Families: offerings that are the same content sold differently (open vs private,
online vs on site, single vs pack) share `Offering.family`.

### Functions

| [`check_card`](_autosummary/pricewright.ratecard.html.md#pricewright.ratecard.check_card)(quotes, \*[, checks])               | Run every check over a card; errors first.                                                                                                                                          |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`dominance`](_autosummary/pricewright.ratecard.html.md#pricewright.ratecard.dominance)(quotes, \*[, slack, fewer])          | An offering that needs clearly fewer hours of work (at most `fewer` x) and no more contact hours than another must not cost more in total (group, event, project or session units). |
| [`effective_rate_spread`](_autosummary/pricewright.ratecard.html.md#pricewright.ratecard.effective_rate_spread)(quotes, \*[, tolerance]) | Every offering should pay the people about the same per hour actually worked.                                                                                                       |
| [`online_vs_onsite`](_autosummary/pricewright.ratecard.html.md#pricewright.ratecard.online_vs_onsite)(quotes)                       | Within a family and unit, the online version should not cost more than the on-site one.                                                                                             |
| [`private_vs_seats`](_autosummary/pricewright.ratecard.html.md#pricewright.ratecard.private_vs_seats)(quotes)                       | A private group should never cost more than buying every seat of the open version.                                                                                                  |
| [`volume_per_hour`](_autosummary/pricewright.ratecard.html.md#pricewright.ratecard.volume_per_hour)(quotes, \*[, slack])           | Within a family and unit, more contact hours should not cost more per hour (packs, longer formats).                                                                                 |

### Classes

| [`Finding`](_autosummary/pricewright.ratecard.html.md#pricewright.ratecard.Finding)(check, severity, message[, offerings])   |    |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----|

# pricewright.report

Render a [`Card`](_autosummary/pricewright.spec.html.md#pricewright.spec.Card) as a Markdown rate card with its rationale.

The page answers, in order: what does each thing cost; is the card consistent; what
does travel add; how do the prices move with the day rate; and, offering by

# _autosummary/pricewright.research.html.md

# pricewright.research

Market research as an input: comparables packets, normalised and compared.

Research is kept apart from the model on purpose. A packet is a YAML (or JSON)
list of comparable prices, gathered by an agent or supplied by the user, in the
schema below; it can be swapped or refreshed without touching any offering.
The model produces a cost-based price; a packet only tells you where that price
sits in the market ([`position()`](_autosummary/pricewright.research.html.md#pricewright.research.position)).

Schema (one record):

```default
id, specialty, offering, provider, region, price | price_low + price_high,
currency, unit, contact_hours, duration_s, group_size, delivery,
provider_tier, evidence (fetched | secondary | snippet | inferred), date, url, notes
```

### Functions

| [`as_is`](_autosummary/pricewright.research.html.md#pricewright.research.as_is)(c)                                        | The price in its own unit (use with a filter that fixes the unit).                         |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`load_packet`](_autosummary/pricewright.research.html.md#pricewright.research.load_packet)(\*paths)                            | Read one or more packets.                                                                  |
| [`per_contact_hour`](_autosummary/pricewright.research.html.md#pricewright.research.per_contact_hour)(c)                             | Price per delivered hour for the whole room (group, event or session prices).              |
| `per_finished_minute`(c)                                                                         |                                                                                            |
| [`per_person_contact_hour`](_autosummary/pricewright.research.html.md#pricewright.research.per_person_contact_hour)(c)                      | Price per participant per delivered hour (needs hours, and a group size for group prices). |
| [`position`](_autosummary/pricewright.research.html.md#pricewright.research.position)(value, comparables, \*[, metric, ...]) | Locate `value` (already in `metric` units and `currency`) among comparables.               |
| `select`(comparables, \*[, specialty, ...])                                                      |                                                                                            |
| [`summary`](_autosummary/pricewright.research.html.md#pricewright.research.summary)(values)                                 | Plain (unweighted) summary, for a quick look at a list of numbers.                         |

### Classes

| [`Comparable`](_autosummary/pricewright.research.html.md#pricewright.research.Comparable)(id, specialty, offering[, price, ...])   |                                                                           |

### pricewright.research.position(value, comparables, , metric='per_person_contact_hour', fx=None, currency='EUR')

Locate `value` (already in `metric` units and `currency`) among comparables.

`fx` maps a currency to its value in `currency` (e.g. `{"USD": 0.87}` when
`currency='EUR'`). A comparable in a currency missing from `fx` is skipped
rather than silently treated as equal.

```pycon
>>> cs = [Comparable(str(i), "training", "x", price=p, unit="per_person",
...                  contact_hours=1, evidence="fetched") for i, p in enumerate([40, 50, 60, 70, 80])]
>>> position(65, cs).verdict, position(65, cs).median
('within market', 60.0)
```

# _autosummary/pricewright.rounding.html.md

# pricewright.rounding

Rounding a computed price to a number a person would print on a rate card.

A computed 2,083.47 is not a price. The default rounds to a step that grows with
the magnitude, so small prices stay precise and large ones look deliberate.
Any `Callable[[float], float]` can replace it (the `rounder=` seam).

### Functions

| [`nice_round`](_autosummary/pricewright.rounding.html.md#pricewright.rounding.nice_round)(x, \*[, steps, up])   | Round `x` to a magnitude-dependent step.                       |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`no_round`](_autosummary/pricewright.rounding.html.md#pricewright.rounding.no_round)(x)                      | The identity rounder, for inspecting the raw cost-plus figure. |

### pricewright.rounding.nice_round(x, , steps=((100, 5), (1000, 10), (5000, 50), (20000, 100), (100000, 500), (inf, 1000)), up=False)

Round `x` to a magnitude-dependent step.

```pycon
>>> nice_round(2083.47)
2100
>>> nice_round(437)
440
>>> nice_round(437, up=True)
440
>>> nice_round(431, up=True)
440
>>> nice_round(87.2)
85
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### pricewright.rounding.no_round(x)

The identity rounder, for inspecting the raw cost-plus figure.

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)


# _autosummary/pricewright.spec.html.md

# pricewright.spec

A rate card as data: one YAML spec in, priced and checked card out.

The spec names the provider’s rates, the offerings (each a specialty template plus
parameters), the research packets to compare against, travel scenarios, and the day
rates to test for sensitivity. [`build_card()`](_autosummary/pricewright.spec.html.md#pricewright.spec.build_card) does the rest. Everything a user
must decide sits in the spec, never in code.

Minimal spec:

```default
title: My rate card
rates: {day_rates: {founder: 900}}
offerings:
  - {id: talk, specialty: training, template: talk}
```

# _autosummary/pricewright.travel.html.md

# pricewright.travel

Travel as explicit variables: time away, nights, subsistence, transport.

An on-site engagement costs the provider three things an online one does not:
**time** (travel hours that could have been billed elsewhere), **nights away**
(when the schedule cannot be done in a day), and **expenses** (transport, hotel,
meals). Industry practice quotes them separately from the professional fee, so a
client in the same city and a client a flight away see the same fee and a
different travel line. This module turns a [`Trip`](_autosummary/pricewright.travel.html.md#pricewright.travel.Trip) into that line, under a
[`TravelPolicy`](_autosummary/pricewright.travel.html.md#pricewright.travel.TravelPolicy) that holds the provider’s terms.

Two ways of billing travel time are in common use, and both are offered:

- `"hourly"`: door-to-door hours beyond a free allowance each way, billed at a
  fraction of the hourly rate (the default fraction is 0.5);
- `"day_blocks"`: each travel leg rounded up to half or full days, billed at a
  fraction of the day rate (speakers and crews often quote a “travel day”).

Expenses are passed through at cost by default (`expense_markup=0`), estimated
up front from the policy’s hotel cap and per diem, and invoiced against receipts.

### Functions

| [`nights_needed`](_autosummary/pricewright.travel.html.md#pricewright.travel.nights_needed)(trip[, policy])           | (night before, night after, total nights) for a trip under a policy.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`travel_addon`](_autosummary/pricewright.travel.html.md#pricewright.travel.travel_addon)(trip, \*[, policy, rates]) | The travel line of a quote: time fee plus estimated expenses.          |

### Classes

| [`TravelPolicy`](_autosummary/pricewright.travel.html.md#pricewright.travel.TravelPolicy)([free_hours_each_way, ...])          | The provider's travel terms.                                               |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TravelQuote`](_autosummary/pricewright.travel.html.md#pricewright.travel.TravelQuote)(trip, policy, nights, days_away, ...) |                                                                            |
| [`Trip`](_autosummary/pricewright.travel.html.md#pricewright.travel.Trip)(one_way_hours[, transport_round_trip, ...])  | One engagement's travel, as the provider would estimate it before quoting. |

# For AI agents

`pricewright` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `pricing-expert`

Price a service or product with a real rationale: a cost-and-effort model at the core (prep and development hours per delivered hour, facilitators or crew, the provider’s day rate, credits and tools, fees, contingency, margin), travel as explicit variables, consistency checks across a whole rate card, and market comparables as a separate, swappable input. Routes by offering type to a specialty: training, talks, workshops, courses and coaching; audiovisual production (commercials, brand films, music videos, animation, documentary, explainers, pilots, retainers); software and apps (subscriptions, pay-as-you-go, credits, seats, freemium, tiers). Use for “price this”, “what should we charge”, “make a rate card”, “is this price consistent”, “day rate”, “how much for a talk / workshop / course / video”, “on-site vs online price”, “travel costs in a quote”, “per diem”, “pricing tiers”, “subscription vs usage pricing”, “credits pricing”, “check our prices against the market”. Backed by the `pricewright` Python package (calculator + CLI).

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/pricewright pricing-expert --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`pricewright/data/skills/pricing-expert`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/pricewright/tree/HEAD/pricewright/data/skills/pricing-expert) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install pricewright`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Subagents

Subagents are Markdown files with a frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `tools`) and a system prompt as the body. Copy one into your project’s `.claude/agents/` (or your agent host’s equivalent) to delegate the task it describes.

### `pricing-expert`

Prices services and products with a real rationale, in a fresh context, and returns a short page plus the path of the full rate card. Use when the user or a session asks what to charge, wants a rate card built or checked for consistency, needs on-site vs online or travel costs in a quote, or wants software/app pricing (subscriptions, usage, credits, tiers). Routes to a specialty (training and workshops; audiovisual production; software and apps), runs or requests the market research, and computes prices with the pricewright package.

Source: [`pricewright/data/agents/pricing-expert.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/pricewright/tree/HEAD/pricewright/data/agents/pricing-expert.md); tools: `Bash, Read, Write, Edit, WebSearch, WebFetch`.

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/pricewright/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`pricewright.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/pricewright/pricewright.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/pricewright/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
